protocolRefs.multiCallChain: HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.

overloadMerges.note: Fixed directions per the parameter table's arrow column: response is filled by the command ('out'), and headerNames/headerValues are read on input (request header names/values) and overwritten on output (response header names/values), so they are 'inout' rather than the mechanical parser's blanket 'in'.

params.name: httpMethod
params.description: HTTP method of the request (e.g. GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE), one of the HTTP Client theme method constants.

params.name: url
params.description: URL to send the request to, e.g. http://[{user}:[{password}]@]host[:{port}][/{path}][?{queryString}].

params.name: contents
params.description: Body of the request; its type selects the default Content-Type sent (text/plain UTF8, application/byte-stream, a picture MIME type, or application/json) when Content-Type isn't explicitly set via headerNames/headerValues.

params.name: response
params.description: Filled with the body of the server response; the variable's type (Text/Blob/Picture/Object/Collection) selects how the raw response is decoded/parsed.

params.name: headerNames
params.description: In: names of request headers to send. Out: overwritten with the names of headers returned by the server.

params.name: headerValues
params.description: In: values of request headers to send. Out: overwritten with the values of headers returned by the server.
If passed, keep the server connection alive after this call instead of closing it automatically.

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Sends an arbitrary HTTP request (any method) with an optional body to a URL and returns the server's response body plus response headers; the function result is the HTTP status code (0 if the connection itself failed).

constraints: If the response variable's type doesn't match the actual result, the mismatched-Object case falls back to returning a 4D.Blob object rather than failing to parse.
A return value of 0 indicates a network-level failure (DNS/unreachable server, not an HTTP error status) and an error is generated, interceptable via ON ERR CALL.
During HTTPS requests, the server certificate's authority is not checked by this command.
